source.title: Understanding Positional Features in Layer 0 SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The note discusses SAE feature geometry and suggests studying feature splitting, but it does not compare dictionary sizes or test any of the listed splitting claims.
record.gate_note: The study examines one gpt2-small SAE with d_sae=24576. It reports positional-feature findings, but does not test whether features split as dictionary size grows. Its length-generalization observations do not measure the listed splitting claims.
record.test_reason: The note studies one gpt2-small layer 0 SAE (d_sae=24576) and its positional features. It compares no dictionary sizes or objectives and checks no hierarchy or absorption. It only suggests that positional embeddings could be a toy setting for studying feature splitting, and predicts that positional feature counts scale predictably with SAE width, without testing this.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also attribute SAE breakdown beyond the training context length to positional features overfitting to short contexts and to the use of absolute positional embeddings.
record.recipe_differences: No comparison of SAE training recipes or dictionary sizes is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: In a gpt2-small layer 0 SAE, about 50 of 24k features are positional. Each covers a range of positions, and early positions get more dedicated features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on absolute positional embeddings tile the positional manifold with range-covering features, more finely where embeddings are more spread out.

record.problems: Only one SAE size is studied, so there is no evidence about how feature organization changes with dictionary size. Uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The note's observations about reconstruction error and feature activations beyond the SAE context length were left out because they do not measure the listed splitting claims.

untested.parts: No comparison across dictionary sizes; the coarse-to-fine prediction is stated, not tested.
No test of nested feature families or concept hierarchy.
No parent/child firing or absorption measurement.
No comparison of latents across SAE sizes.
Sparsity penalty offered as an explanation for range-covering features, but no objective comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong note covering a single SAE. The rows are correctly linked to no version.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE dictionary-size comparison or measurement of coarse-to-fine feature replacement, input coverage, or directional proximity.
No scaling comparison, large-model study, or comparison across open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families or whether they mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
No parent-child latent firing comparison or test of whether SAE size or sparsity changes absorption.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latent combinations or novel latents.
No test of whether the SAE objective produces splitting, or comparison with Matryoshka or another objective.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Counted features with high positional scores in the layer 0 SAE.
rows.value: There seem to be only ~50 positional features (of 24k total features).
rows.note: This is a count for one SAE, not a comparison across dictionary sizes.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the positions at which layer 0 SAE positional features activate.
rows.measure: Distribution of positional feature activations across positions
rows.value: Many positional features span the entire context length; later positions share features across several positions, while early positions get proportionally more dedicated features.
rows.note: The note attributes the pattern to the ground-truth positional embeddings being more spread out for early positions; this is not a test of feature splitting across SAE sizes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
